questions.question: What is the consequence of losing your Android app's signing keystore?
options: Nothing significant, a new keystore can be generated and used immediately
You cannot publish further updates to the existing app listing under the same package name — you'd need to create an entirely new listing
The app will stop working for existing users immediately
Google automatically recovers lost keystores from backups
questions.explanation: The Play Store ties an app's identity to its original signing key; without it, there's no way to prove a new build is the legitimate continuation of the existing app.

questions.question: What must be true of Android's versionCode and iOS's build number on every single submission, including a minor bug-fix resubmission?
options: They can stay the same as long as the human-readable version string changes
They must strictly increase with every submission, even if nothing else about the release notes changed
They only need to increase for major version releases
They are optional metadata with no enforcement
questions.explanation: Both stores require this internal build identifier to increase on every submission — forgetting to bump it is a common cause of first-time submission rejections.

questions.question: Which of these changes CANNOT be shipped via an OTA update like Expo Updates or CodePush?
options: A JS bug fix in a checkout flow
Adding a new native module that requires a new device permission
questions.explanation: OTA updates can only replace the JS bundle and assets the native shell already knows how to load — any change to native code or permissions requires a full store review.

questions.question: Why might a team choose a tool like EAS Build to manage code signing credentials?
options: It removes the need for any code signing entirely
It handles much of the manual certificate/provisioning-profile/keystore management that would otherwise be done by hand
It bypasses Apple's and Google's review processes
It is required for an app to run on a physical device during development
questions.explanation: Managing provisioning profiles, certificates, and keystores by hand is a common first-time pain point; managed build services can handle much of that complexity on a team's behalf.
